title: Read the Ruin: Which Layer?
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Place twelve things seen on Day 2 in Istanbul into the Roman, Byzantine, Latin occupation, Ottoman or Republic layer in which they arrived, including three trap cards made long before they arrived.

learningObjectives: Apply the rule "a thing belongs to the layer in which it arrived at this place" to assign twelve things seen on Day 2 to one of five historical layers, with at least 10 of 12 correct on the first attempt, including at least 2 of the 3 trap cards.
prerequisites: The four ways a layer is added: built over, reused, converted, removed
The Roman, Byzantine, Ottoman and Republic eras

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Rule-based classification practice with immediate feedback (sorting)
keyQuestions: In which layer did this arrive?
When was it made, and when did it arrive here?
Which of the four ways added this layer?
commonMisconceptions: An object belongs to the era in which it was made.
Anything that looks European and modern must be from the Republic.
Everything in Hagia Sophia is Byzantine.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score on twelve cards (mastery: 10 of 12, with at least 2 of 3 trap cards).
Name the three Byzantine-layer objects that are much older than Byzantium.
Place the Blue Mosque and the Library of Celsus statues in their layers.
